holidays.name: TV Dinner Day
holidays.description: A salute to the frozen, compartmentalized meal that let families eat in front of the television. Celebrate by peeling back the foil on a tray of mystery-flavored mashed potatoes and a tiny brownie.
holidays.origin: The date is an unofficial food observance honoring the TV dinner, which was popularized by Swanson in the 1950s. The company's 1953 Thanksgiving-style turkey tray became a huge hit as TV sets entered American homes.
holidays.funFact: Swanson reportedly overestimated its Thanksgiving turkey supply in 1953 and was left with about 260 tons of frozen turkey, which inspired the idea of packaging it into trays with sides.

holidays.name: World Suicide Prevention Day
holidays.description: An international awareness day dedicated to promoting understanding, reducing stigma, and encouraging support and conversation around mental health. Many people light candles at 8 p.m. in remembrance and hope.
holidays.origin: Established in 2003 by the International Association for Suicide Prevention in collaboration with the World Health Organization. It is observed worldwide each September 10.
holidays.funFact: The day's signature ritual is lighting a candle near a window at 8 p.m. local time, creating a wave of light that moves around the globe as time zones shift.

holidays.name: Swap Ideas Day
holidays.description: A day for trading thoughts, brainstorming with friends, and borrowing someone else's brilliant idea. Think of it as a flea market for your brain, with no haggling required.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that encourages collaboration and creative exchange, often celebrated by workplaces, classrooms, and clubs looking to shake up routine thinking.
holidays.funFact: Researchers who study creativity often find that combining ideas from different people and fields leads to more novel solutions than working in isolation.

holidays.name: Sewing Machine Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the humble machine that stitched together the modern clothing industry. Dust off the bobbin, thread the needle, and hem those pants you have been ignoring for six months.
holidays.origin: The date commemorates the 1846 patent awarded to Elias Howe for his lockstitch sewing machine design, a pivotal moment in the history of textile manufacturing.
holidays.funFact: Elias Howe reportedly got the idea of placing the eye of the needle near its point after a dream in which he was threatened by cannibals carrying spears with holes in their tips.
